title: The Unencrypted Secrets Vault
description: An application secrets bucket stores sensitive API tokens and private keys without mandatory Server-Side Encryption (SSE-KMS), violating cryptographic compliance mandates.
scenario: FinTech subsidiary 'VaultCorp' stores production JWT signing keys and customer database credentials in an S3 bucket. Security auditors discovered that the bucket does not enforce Server-Side Encryption with AWS Key Management Service Customer Managed Keys (SSE-KMS), allowing unencrypted writes and lacking automated key rotation.

hints.content: In AWS S3, unencrypted object writes can be prevented at both the bucket configuration layer (Default Encryption) and via an explicit Deny bucket policy requiring the 's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption' header.
Check both the default encryption algorithm ('aws:kms') and ensure a Customer Managed Key (CMK) ARN is specified rather than the default managed key 'aws/s3'.
Enable S3 Bucket Keys to reduce AWS KMS request costs by up to 99%, and verify that automatic annual key rotation is enabled on the underlying KMS key.
Set SSEAlgorithm to 'aws:kms', provide KMSMasterKeyId 'arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/vault-prod-key', set BucketKeyEnabled=True, EnforceKMSSSEPolicy=True, and KMSKeyRotationEnabled=True.
